title: Target anatomy
view: Transverse section of the right groin at the femoral crease under a linear probe, seen from the feet as on ultrasound: lateral on the image left, medial on the right.
teachingPoint: The femoral nerve lies lateral to the artery, under the fascia iliaca, on the iliopsoas; the needle comes in-plane from lateral and its tip passes through the fascia iliaca beside the nerve, where the injectate surrounds it.
claims: Right groin in section, seen from the feet: lateral on the left, the same way round as the positioning plate. Adapted from the approved FICB layout.
Femoral nerve lateral to the femoral artery, deep to the fascia iliaca, in the plane on the iliopsoas, not in the muscle (record, anatomy).
Femoral vein medial to the artery; both superficial to the fascia iliaca (standard anatomy, added).
Needle in-plane from lateral to medial, tip through the fascia iliaca beside the nerve (record, steps 4-5).
Teal: injectate under the fascia iliaca surrounding the femoral nerve, not reaching the artery (record, steps 6).
Four labels: Fascia iliaca, Femoral nerve, Femoral artery, Iliopsoas.
